ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A cylindrical thermally conductive cylinder has a length of $L_{0}=60\mathrm{cm}$. A certain mass of ideal gas is enclosed within the cylinder by a massless and infinitesimally thin piston. A trigger D is installed at the bottom of the cylinder, which is activated when the pressure inside the cylinder reaches $p=1.5 \times 10^{5}\mathrm{{Pa}}$. The friction between the piston and the cylinder wall is negligible. Initially, the piston is located at the opening of the cylinder, the ambient temperature is $t_{0}=27^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, and the ambient pressure is $p_{0}=1.0 \times 10^{5}\mathrm{{Pa}}$.

1. If the ambient temperature remains constant, and the piston is slowly pushed downwards, determine the distance from the piston to the bottom of the cylinder when D is just triggered.
2. If the piston is fixed at the opening of the cylinder, and the ambient temperature is slowly increased, determine the ambient temperature when D is just triggered.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The contents of the two attached figures are the same. In the figure is a vertically placed cylinder whose cross-section remains unchanged along the height; there is a black piston at the upper opening, and on the left a double-headed arrow marks the full length L0 from the upper end to the bottom; on the right side of the cylinder bottom there is a trigger marked D. Since the cross-sectional area of the cylinder is unchanged, the gas volume can be written as V=A×gas-column height. Reasoning: In the initial state, the piston is at the opening, the gas height is L0=60 cm=0.60 m, the pressure is p0=1.0×10^5 Pa, and the temperature is T0=27℃=300 K. When trigger D is triggered, the gas pressure is p=1.5×10^5 Pa=1.5p0. Question 1: The ambient temperature is unchanged and the compression is slow, so the gas undergoes an isothermal change and satisfies Boyle's law p0 V0=pV. Let the distance from the piston to the bottom when triggered be x, then V0=AL0, V=Ax, so p0AL0=pAx, obtaining x=(p0/p)L0=L0/1.5=0.60/1.5=0.40 m. Question 2: The piston is fixed at the opening, and the gas volume remains AL0 unchanged; the cylinder conducts heat and is heated slowly, so the gas temperature is equal to the ambient temperature. The constant-volume process satisfies p/T=p0/T0, so T=(p/p0)T0=1.5×300 K=450 K.
